messages:
amanda: Heads up — planning KMS integration pattern for Redwood Private (VPC) control plane + data-plane. Thinking about a lightweight KMS proxy that handles grants + envelope key caching. Need feedback on rotation, audit surface, and RBAC changes.

kevin: +1 on proxy for control plane. avoids exposing AWS creds to every service. question: will proxy hold DEKs in memory? how do we handle restarts? :thinking:

sanjay: We should treat proxy as a short-lived credential broker, not long-term key storage. caching is fine but must be TTL + evict on SIGTERM. Use envelope keys in KMS, data-plane uses DEK ephemeral in memory only.

eli: For rotation, prefer staged rewrap: new CMK -> rewrap DEKs -> update metadata. Avoid re-encrypting large blobs in-place during business hours. schedule canary rewraps for low-traffic shards.

lisa: RBAC changes: service accounts that call the proxy need kms:Decrypt on grant-created keys? or should proxy hold a cross-account grant and make Decrypt calls on behalf?

kevin: Proxy holds IAM role with kms:Decrypt/kms:Encrypt and uses grants to limit scope. Services never get direct AWS keys. Proxy returns encrypted DEK blob + metadata. Services use local DEK cache to decrypt with proxy call.

amanda: Sketch of flow:
```
1) Create CMK in customer account (BYOK optional)
2) Proxy assumes role with limited kms permissions and Grant management
3) Client service requests DEK for object X -> proxy generates DEK, Encrypt with CMK -> returns {ciphertext_blob, dek_id, expiry}
4) Client caches DEK in memory for TTL, uses it to encrypt local data
5) On rotation, proxy rewraps ciphertext_blob under new CMK & rotates dek_id metadata
```

sanjay: Add audit events for every Grant create/destroy and every Decrypt call. Push to central audit log (immutable). Add TTL to grants so accidental long-lived grants auto-expire.

eli: Important: ensure crypto transition is atomic for readers. Have both old/new dek metadata for a window and route decrypts accordingly.

lisa: For emergency revocation (compromise), playbook: revoke grants -> revoke proxy role sessions -> rotate CMK -> rewrap critical DEKs. Keep pageable runbook with commands.

devsec-bot: Reminder: check compliance matrix — PCI/ISO require key rotation policies and retained audit trails. See /docs/compliance/kms-playbook.

oncall-bot: Incident runbook link: https://wiki.internal/runbooks/kms-compromise — notify secops, spin read-only fallback, enable fallback cipher variant.

kevin: One edge case: large state stores where DEKs wrap thousands of objects. Rewrap at metadata layer: keep object pointers to ciphertext + dek_id; rewrap asynchronously and mark objects as migrated. readers check latest dek_id and attempt rewrap if stale.

amanda: What about cross-region? We plan to keep CMKs per-region and use cross-account grants for DR. Proxy should prefer local CMK for latency.

sanjay: Agree. Also keep a region-to-CMK mapping in config store and replicate mapping via signed metadata.

eli: Anything on key-rotation automation? AWS KMS automatic rotation only for symmetric CMKs — not sufficient for staged rewrap. Suggest we run a rotation orchestrator: 1) create new CMK 2) create grants 3) rewrap sample -> smoke -> bulk async rewrap -> retire old CMK. All steps logged.

lisa: RBAC delta: need a migration for service roles to drop kms:Decrypt and instead call proxy endpoint. Update Terraform modules and run a rollout with canaries.

amanda: Ok next steps: draft proxy design doc + rotation orchestrator runbook. @kevin @sanjay volunteer to own POC. @lisa can you draft RBAC/Terraform changes?

kevin: I can do POC for proxy (Go) — will include graceful shutdown caching and grant TTL management.

sanjay: I'll work on orchestrator and audit plumbing.

lisa: Will update TF modules and prepare staged rollout plan.

amanda: Great. I'll create a GH issue and a short timeline. thanks all :raised_hands:)
